comment: Shared verdict-key vector for the NVD window and baseline checkpoint verdicts a satellite stamps on the vulnerability.source_snapshot payload and the Eshu core extension host reads (eshu-hq/eshu-sdk#93, eshu-hq/eshu#10732). Reader: eshu go/internal/collector/extensionhost nvd_window_cursor.go (armNVDWindowCursorWriter) and nvd_baseline_cursor.go (NVDBaselineCommitPolicy.CommitPolicy), read at eshu origin/main f6c9b68d4d5d9b4ef39b5490b1109cc7f1e4b1c2 and replayed unchanged at 6bf9450d7acb. Writers: eshu-collector-vulnerability-intelligence origin/main ffbeade7d38374d0bec8d2c4e6f327d7bd6f99ac for the window keys (stampNVDWindowVerdict, decideNVDWindowAdvance) and, for the baseline keys, its unmerged branch drive/158-nvd-baseline-snapshot-keys at 6965a17 (nvdBaselineSnapshot), because collector main does not yet stamp them. Numbers are plain JSON numbers because the claim transport decodes them as float64. expect.advance_to, expect.head and expect.year_complete are what the armed commit-transaction writer carries, and 0, 0 and false when no writer is armed. A case's malformed_keys names payload keys that deliberately carry the wrong JSON type. emitted_by_collector is true only when a real collector builder can stamp exactly that payload, except on the position cases named below, where it states the shape the collector change must stamp; false marks a reader pin that exercises core on input the collector never emits. Position keys (eshu-hq/eshu-sdk#97, ruling for eshu-hq/eshu#10671): nvd_baseline_advance_to_cve_id and nvd_baseline_year_generated_unix_us, the four-segment baseline scope, and the top-level position block are the shape ruled for the baseline resume position. No collector builder stamps them yet (the collector change is eshu-hq/eshu-collector-vulnerability-intelligence#199) and core does not read them yet (eshu-hq/eshu#10809, eshu-hq/eshu#10810), so emitted_by_collector on a case that carries them, and on the four older emitted baseline cases that gained year_generated_unix_us, states the shape that change must stamp, not what any collector main stamps today. expect.advance_to_cve_id and expect.year_generated_unix_us are optional members: absent reads as an empty id and 0. Payload keys that ride on the same snapshot but are outside this vector: nvd_keyed, nvd_transport, nvd_feed_selector, nvd_feed_time_unix_us, nvd_feed_span_start_unix_us, nvd_feed_sha256.

keys.name: nvd_window_advance_to_unix_us
keys.note: The next cursor. 0 when should_advance is false. Core arms nothing when it is not positive.

keys.name: nvd_window_head_unix_us
keys.note: The server catalog head the advance was clamped to. 0 when unknown.

keys.name: nvd_window_should_advance
keys.note: Strict: only the JSON boolean true can move the cursor. The string "true" holds.

keys.name: nvd_window_time_anomaly_reason
keys.note: Pinned, not read by core: a hold rides on should_advance false. Empty when the observation is clean.

keys.name: nvd_window_pages_refetched
keys.note: Informational, not read by core, not cased: window pages refetched after a retryable failure.

keys.name: nvd_window_pages_downsized
keys.note: Informational, not read by core, not cased: window pages refetched at a halved size after an oversize page.

keys.name: nvd_window_split
keys.note: Informational, not read by core, not cased: stamped true on a claim that was split across the feed or the API.

keys.name: nvd_window_retry_reason
keys.note: Informational, not read by core, not cased: present only when the window refetched from its minted start.

cases.name: advances
cases.note: A clean window: should_advance true, a positive advance_to, the server head. The writer is armed with both.

cases.name: advances_clamped_to_head
cases.note: The collector clamps advance_to to min(planned end, head), so a head before the window end is the advance.

cases.name: advances_with_record_beyond_head_anomaly
cases.note: A time anomaly alone never holds the cursor: the reader does not read time_anomaly_reason.

cases.name: holds_head_unknown
cases.note: No server head, so the collector stamps should_advance false with advance_to and head 0. Facts commit, the cursor holds.

cases.name: holds_head_behind_cursor
cases.note: The server head reads at or before the window start: the collector holds rather than moving the cursor backward.

cases.name: holds_should_advance_false
cases.note: Reader pin, not a shape the collector emits: should_advance false holds even beside a positive advance_to.

cases.name: holds_zero_advance_to
cases.note: Reader pin, not a shape the collector emits: should_advance true with advance_to 0 is degenerate and arms nothing.

cases.name: holds_string_should_advance
cases.note: The verdict is strict: the string "true" is not the boolean true, so the cursor holds.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_run
keys.note: Informational, not read by core: the run id is parsed from the scope id.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_year
keys.note: Informational, not read by core: the year is parsed from the scope id.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_advance_to_unix_us
keys.note: The resume stamp: the exclusive upper bound of what the chunk emitted and the inclusive lower bound of the next chunk. Core floors it to a whole millisecond. With advance_to_cve_id it is the stamp half of the resume position.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_advance_to_cve_id
keys.note: The id half of the resume position (advance_to, advance_to_cve_id): the first record this chunk did not emit, an inclusive lower bound for the next chunk. Present only when that position is inside an instant, that is when the chunk was cut between two records that share the stamp advance_to. Absent means the empty id, so an empty id is never stamped as an empty string. A canonical id is trimmed, upper-cased and matches [A-Z0-9-]{1,64}; ids compare by byte order, so CVE-2025-10000 sorts before CVE-2025-9999 (see the position block). Core requires an incomplete verdict to move strictly forward in (advance_to, advance_to_cve_id) order; a complete verdict may equal its start. How core treats a value that is not a canonical id is not pinned here.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_year_sha256
keys.note: The seed year file identity: 64 lowercase hex characters once surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Anything else covers nothing.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_year_generated_unix_us
keys.note: The seed manifest lastModified for the year, in unix microseconds, stamped beside year_sha256 so the checkpoint writer can refuse a seed rollback at commit. That guard compares against the stored checkpoint, so it is a commit-transaction refusal and not an outcome this vector can name. expect.year_generated_unix_us carries the stamped value on an advanced case. How core treats an absent or non-positive stamp is not pinned here.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_year_complete
keys.note: True when the chunk finished the year. A complete chunk may land exactly on its start.

keys.name: nvd_baseline_should_advance
keys.note: Strict: only the JSON boolean true can advance the checkpoint.

cases.name: advances_past_start
cases.note: An incomplete chunk that moves strictly past its start: the checkpoint is armed to advance_to.

cases.name: advances_complete_past_start
cases.note: A year-complete chunk past its start.

cases.name: advances_complete_at_start
cases.note: A complete chunk may land exactly on its start: it resumed at the stream tail and has no later stamp to name.

cases.name: advances_sub_millisecond_floors
cases.note: advance_to is floored to a whole millisecond, never rounded up, so a stored resume can only re-read.

cases.name: not_covered_incomplete_at_start
cases.note: Reader pin, not a shape the collector emits (it stamps should_advance false here): an incomplete chunk that does not move past its start would re-mint the same scope forever.

cases.name: not_covered_sub_millisecond_floors_to_start
cases.note: The floor applies before the comparison, so a sub-millisecond lead over the start is no progress.

cases.name: not_covered_behind_start
cases.note: No verdict may move behind the chunk start.

cases.name: not_covered_complete_behind_start
cases.note: A complete verdict is also refused behind the start: the behind-start check comes first.

cases.name: not_covered_missing_advance
cases.note: should_advance true without an advance_to stamp.

cases.name: not_covered_zero_advance
cases.note: A non-positive advance_to is missing.

cases.name: not_covered_string_advance
cases.note: advance_to must be a JSON number; a string is missing.

cases.name: not_covered_sha_blank
cases.note: A blank seed sha names nothing the next plan can pin.

cases.name: not_covered_sha_malformed
cases.note: The seed sha is 64 lowercase hex characters; uppercase is malformed.

cases.name: advances_sha_with_surrounding_whitespace
cases.note: Core trims surrounding whitespace from the seed sha before the 64-hex check and stores the trimmed value, so padded input is accepted.

cases.name: holds_should_advance_false
cases.note: The no-progress shape: an incomplete chunk that resumed at its own start and found nothing past it. should_advance is false, so facts commit and the checkpoint holds.

cases.name: holds_string_should_advance
cases.note: The verdict is strict: the string "true" is not the boolean true.

cases.name: holds_no_snapshot_keys
cases.note: A snapshot that carries only identity keys has no verdict, so the checkpoint holds.

cases.name: refused_window_verdict_present
cases.note: A baseline generation carrying a window advance verdict is refused and nothing commits: a baseline chunk never arms the window cursor writer.

cases.name: refused_window_verdict_beside_baseline_hold
cases.note: The window-verdict refusal comes before the baseline should_advance check, so a baseline hold does not hide it.

cases.name: advances_cut_inside_instant
cases.note: The chunk was cut between two records that share the stamp advance_to: the position is (advance_to, CVE-2025-1500), so the id rides beside the stamp. The scope is the three-segment form because the start has no id.

cases.name: advances_whole_instant_cut_inside
cases.note: A chunk that ended on an instant boundary leaves a three-segment start at the instant T. The next chunk is cut inside that same instant, so it advances to (T, id) at the same stamp: the shape a large same-stamp group takes while it drains across chunks.

cases.name: advances_within_instant_by_cve_id
cases.note: Resumed inside the instant and cut inside it again: the stamp ties with the start, so the id alone moves the position strictly forward.

cases.name: advances_instant_drained
cases.note: Resumed inside an instant and drained it: the next position is a later whole instant, so advance_to_cve_id is absent, not an empty string.

cases.name: advances_id_byte_order_past_numeric
cases.note: Ids order by bytes: CVE-2025-9999 sorts after CVE-2025-10000 even though it is numerically smaller, so this is forward progress.

cases.name: advances_complete_at_position
cases.note: A complete chunk may land exactly on its start position, id included: it resumed at the stream tail and has nothing later to name.

cases.name: holds_no_progress_at_position
cases.note: The no-progress shape at a four-segment start: an incomplete chunk that found nothing past its own position stamps should_advance false.

cases.name: not_covered_same_position_incomplete
cases.note: Reader pin, not a shape the collector emits (it stamps should_advance false here): an incomplete chunk whose position ties its start would re-mint the same scope forever.

cases.name: not_covered_id_behind_position
cases.note: Same stamp, smaller id: no verdict may move behind the start position.

cases.name: not_covered_dropped_id_behind_position
cases.note: The empty id sorts before every id, so (T, empty) is behind (T, id): dropping the id from a verdict resumed inside the instant moves backward.

cases.name: not_covered_complete_dropped_id_behind_position
cases.note: A complete verdict may equal its start but never sit behind it: (T, empty) is behind (T, id).

cases.name: not_covered_id_numeric_order_behind_position
cases.note: Byte order, not numeric order: CVE-2025-10000 sorts before CVE-2025-9999, so it is behind this start.

position.comment: The NVD baseline resume position (eshu-hq/eshu-sdk#97, ruling for eshu-hq/eshu#10671): the pair (start_unix_us, from_cve_id) that a baseline scope id names and a baseline verdict advances. Core and the collector each implement the scope parser, the scope builder, the id canonicalization and the order, and replay these cases against them. A position has exactly one scope id: the start stamp is a canonical decimal int64 (no leading zeros, no overflow) and the id is the fourth segment only when it is not empty. A scope id always carries the canonical id as is; the canonicalization applies to record ids read from the feed. An inclusive lower bound, not a pointer to a record: the next chunk starts at the first record at or after the position.
position.cve_id_canonical: trim Unicode white space (strings.TrimSpace semantics), reject any non-ASCII byte, upper-case ASCII letters, then require cve_id_pattern
position.order: start_unix_us ascending as an integer, then from_cve_id by unsigned byte order; the empty id sorts before every id

canonical_ids.name: canonical_unchanged
canonical_ids.note: An id already canonical is unchanged.

canonical_ids.name: newline_trimmed
canonical_ids.note: Trailing Unicode white space is trimmed, as strings.TrimSpace does.

canonical_ids.name: carriage_return_trimmed
canonical_ids.note: Carriage returns are white space and are trimmed.

canonical_ids.name: nbsp_trimmed
canonical_ids.note: U+00A0 is Unicode white space, so strings.TrimSpace trims it before the ASCII check; only a non-ASCII byte left after the trim is rejected.

canonical_ids.name: lowercase_upper_cased
canonical_ids.note: A record id is upper-cased. A scope id never carries the lowercase form.

canonical_ids.name: tab_and_space_trimmed
canonical_ids.note: Surrounding space and tab are trimmed. A scope id never carries the padded form.

canonical_ids.name: longest_64
canonical_ids.note: 64 characters is the longest canonical id.

canonical_ids.name: blank
canonical_ids.note: A blank id is not canonical; an empty position id is written as no id at all.

canonical_ids.name: overlong_65
canonical_ids.note: 65 characters is over the length bound.

canonical_ids.name: underscore
canonical_ids.note: Only A-Z, 0-9 and the hyphen are allowed.

canonical_ids.name: non_ascii_upper_cases_to_ascii
canonical_ids.note: U+017F upper-cases to the ASCII letter S under unicode rules, so it is rejected before upper-casing, not after.

round_trips.name: three_segment_empty_id
round_trips.note: An empty id is never written as a trailing segment: the position (T, empty) has exactly this one scope id.

round_trips.name: four_segment
round_trips.note: A position inside an instant adds the canonical id as the fourth segment.

rejections.name: empty_trailing_segment
rejections.note: An empty id is never a trailing segment; the three-segment form is the only encoding of an empty id.

rejections.name: lowercase_id
rejections.note: The scope carries the canonical id, so the lowercase form names no position.

rejections.name: padded_id_leading
rejections.note: A padded id is not canonical.

rejections.name: padded_id_newline
rejections.note: A scope id is already canonical, so any white space is rejected, including a newline.

rejections.name: padded_id_nbsp
rejections.note: A scope id is already canonical, so U+00A0 is rejected even though a record id would trim it.

rejections.name: leading_zero_start
rejections.note: The start is a canonical decimal, so a leading zero would give one position a second scope id.

rejections.name: overflow_start
rejections.note: The start must fit an int64; 9223372036854775808 does not.

rejections.name: padded_id_trailing
rejections.note: A padded id is not canonical.

rejections.name: overlong_id
rejections.note: 65 characters is over the length bound.

rejections.name: non_ascii_id_upper_cases_to_ascii
rejections.note: U+017F upper-cases to S: it must not be admitted by upper-casing first.

rejections.name: extra_segment
rejections.note: A scope has at most four position segments.

rejections.name: id_in_start_slot
rejections.note: An id cannot stand in for the start stamp.

rejections.name: non_numeric_start
rejections.note: The start is decimal digits only.

orders.name: id_ten_thousand_before_nine_thousand
orders.note: Byte order, not numeric order: the byte 1 sorts before 9, so CVE-2025-10000 comes before CVE-2025-9999.

orders.name: id_nine_thousand_after_ten_thousand
orders.note: The same pair reversed: byte order makes CVE-2025-9999 the later position.

orders.name: empty_id_before_any_id
orders.note: At one stamp the whole instant (empty id) sorts before every position inside it.

orders.name: later_stamp_beats_id
orders.note: The stamp compares first, as an integer: any position in a later instant is later, whatever the ids.

orders.name: equal_position
orders.note: One position compares equal to itself.

orders.name: equal_empty_position
orders.note: Two whole-instant positions at one stamp compare equal.

orders.name: shorter_prefix_first
orders.note: An id that is a prefix of another sorts first.

orders.name: hyphen_before_digit
orders.note: The hyphen byte 0x2D sorts before a digit, which a linguistic collation can order differently; core stores the id with a byte-order collation.

orders.name: letter_after_digit
orders.note: Upper-case letters follow digits in byte order.
